docs(v2.14): placeholder cycle plan (Starlight migration)

Tentative v2.14.0 theme: doc-stack migration from MkDocs Material
to Astro Starlight, contingent on a Day-1 60-min compatibility
spike outcome.

Plan structure
- Theme: tentative "Doc Stack: Starlight Migration" pending
  spike GO / GO-WITH-CAVEATS / NO-GO verdict.
- Bucket A: Starlight spike Day 1 (rubric reused verbatim from
  v2.13 Zensical spike with the candidate name swapped).
- Bucket B: migration execution if GO (1-2 weeks: config
  rewrite, content collections, theme port, generator
  verification, redirects port, CI integration, Pages deploy).
- Bucket C: pivot scope if NO-GO (sample-automation slate,
  meeting-lifecycle workflow, CI doc-cleanup mini-bucket,
  GitHub-platform metadata work, F-37, etc.).

Why Starlight over alternatives
- Solves both v2.13 Zensical BLOCKERs cleanly (first-class
  redirects config; sane excludes via draft frontmatter and
  path-based config).
- Production-ready since v1.0 (Sept 2024); used by Cloudflare
  Workers, Deno, Tauri, Astro docs.
- Faster builds, smaller user-side JS payload, modern
  accessibility and web-standards defaults.
- Markdown + MDX first-class; source SKILL.md files don't need
  rewriting; generated content from Python scripts works
  unchanged.
- Node-only toolchain (no Python dependency).

Why both spike + migration in same cycle (v2.14)
- v2.13 split spike from migration because v2.13 had OTHER
  scope (Bucket A doc cleanup, Bucket C CI hardening) that
  shipped regardless. v2.14 doesn't have that other-scope
  cushion.
- Spike report is planning material, not user-value; shipping
  a release whose only output is "we evaluated and decided"
  is an anti-pattern.
- Single-cycle pattern: spike Day 1, decision, migration or
  pivot. Same shape as how v2.13 ran the Zensical spike, just
  without extra non-spike scope.

  references/{TEMPLATE,EXAMPLE}.md, and sample_*.md scope
- Updates spec acceptance criteria #7 + #8 with verified status and a
  post-merge addendum documenting the regression and fix

Manual break test confirms the new lint check catches the defect class:
inject unquoted colon, lint exits 1 with parse-error message; restore,
lint exits 0.

fix(v2.14): FU6 close bash/pwsh parity + 7 broken links + promote check-internal-link-validity to truly enforcing

Closes Codex PR.2 P1.1 finding (validator enforcement claim mismatch)
end-to-end. The 'parity gap' surfaced in W13 B3.5 was actually a
Windows Git Bash locale issue, not a script logic bug. Bash + pwsh
both detect all 7 broken links once the locale is set; the broken
links themselves were generator-output and EXAMPLE.md illustrative-
link defects.

Root cause of locale issue: 'grep -P' (Perl regex) requires UTF-8
locale. On Windows Git Bash with empty default LANG/LC_ALL, grep -P
silently fails with 'supports only unibyte and UTF-8 locales' and
returns no matches. The bash validator silently reported 0 broken
links because the link extraction step never ran. CI Linux runners
use C.UTF-8 by default and would have caught the broken links if
--strict had been set.

Fixes:

1) scripts/check-internal-link-validity.sh: prepend
   export LC_ALL=${LC_ALL:-C.UTF-8} so Windows Git Bash testing
   does not silently false-pass. Closes the script-author trap
   that produced this whole chain.

2) scripts/generate-skill-pages.py: add rewrite_internal_paths()

feat(foundation-sprint-skills): add tool-foundation-sprint-magic-lenses

candidate approaches, pattern review, top bet + backup selection.

Required lenses: 4 classic (customer, pragmatic, growth, money) plus

The skill produces qualitative dot-position scoring rather than numeric
precision; arbitrary numeric precision is treated as a smell. Pattern
review surfaces consistent winners, consistent losers (eliminated),
contradictions, and the biggest trade-off the Decider must take.

Top bet AND backup plan are both required outputs. Backup must be
strategically distinct from top bet (not an iteration). Without explicit
backup, invalidation of the top bet sends the team back to ambiguous
debate.

- Treating lens scoring as math (3.7 vs 3.8 arguments)
- Skipping the custom lens (classic 4 are generic by design)
- Falling in love with the top bet
- Backup too similar to top bet
- Decider picks before pattern review

  * "chain composition: auditor inlined"   (THE failing colon - YAML reads as new mapping key)

description value, producing "bad indentation of a mapping entry" error
at parse position 199.

preserve the existing inner double-quoted phrase ("reference + execute
inline") without escaping; YAML treats colons inside single-quoted scalars
as plain text.

fix(v2.16.0-ao-drift): broken links in dispatch generated pages + generator sub-agent-command count (DM8 absorption)

Two related fixes; both close check-internal-link-validity + check-count-consistency
failures on spike PR #147 CI surfaced by pre-tag-validate.sh.

PART 1 - Broken link fix (12 links across 4 dispatch skills + their references):

The 4 dispatch skills' SKILL.md + references/EXAMPLE.md + references/TEMPLATE.md
files contained markdown links to sibling files using relative paths that worked
from the source location (e.g., `[\`references/TEMPLATE.md\`](./references/TEMPLATE.md)`
resolves from skills/utility-pm-X/SKILL.md to skills/utility-pm-X/references/TEMPLATE.md).
The generator (scripts/generate-skill-pages.py) copies the content to
docs/skills/utility/utility-pm-X.md where the same relative paths break:
`./references/TEMPLATE.md` from docs/skills/utility/ resolves to
docs/skills/utility/references/TEMPLATE.md which does not exist.

Same class for EXAMPLE.md embedded "Related Files" sections: links like
`[\`SKILL.md\`](../SKILL.md)` work from skills/utility-pm-X/references/EXAMPLE.md
but break when embedded into docs/skills/utility/utility-pm-X.md.

Fix: 12 markdown links converted to plain code spans
(e.g., `[\`SKILL.md\`](../SKILL.md)` to `\`SKILL.md\``). Preserves the file
reference for human readers while avoiding markdown link resolution. Acceptable
trade-off: dispatch skill "Related Files" sections are descriptive, not
navigational; the canonical navigation goes through subagents/ or the
runtime-components.md catalog.

  * skills/utility-pm-critic/SKILL.md                       (2 links)
  * skills/utility-pm-critic/references/EXAMPLE.md          (2 links)
  * skills/utility-pm-critic/references/TEMPLATE.md         (1 link)

scripts/generate-skill-pages.py previously computed total_cmd_count as

fix(v2.16.0-codex-review): address 6 codex adversarial review findings (1 P1 + 2 P2 + 3 P3)

Codex adversarial review of the 14-commit doc-stack spike (HEAD 92e1448)
returned 6 actionable findings; all addressed in this commit.

P1 - README.md historical count corruption (bulk count sweep regression):

  The bulk count sweep (commit `197d352`) used Python text replacement that
  did not respect the `<!-- count-exempt:start --> ... <!-- count-exempt:end -->`
  blocks the check-count-consistency validator honors. Line 224 of README.md
  sits inside the block at lines 136-276 ("Previous Release Details") which
  is historical content protected from staleness sweeps.

  Sweep falsified the historical snapshot:
    Before: "Current totals at v2.15.0: 59 skills, 66 commands, 12 workflows"
    Truth at v2.15.0 ship: 55 skills + 62 commands
    Fixed:  "Totals at v2.15.0: 55 skills, 62 commands, 12 workflows; see
             latest release notes for the current catalog state."

  Rephrasing clarifies that these are point-in-time snapshots at v2.15.0;
  current catalog is at 59/66/12 (visible in non-historical sections).

  Root-cause learning for future bulk sweeps: replace-all helpers must
  respect count-exempt markers OR use the validator's exempt-block parsing
  logic OR sweep only validator-flagged lines (not raw text replacement
  across full file content). Future helper scripts should encode this.

P2 - SKILL.md terminology now inconsistent with AGENTS.md + commands/release.md:

  Commit `fa5ed8b` changed `skills/utility-pm-release-conductor/SKILL.md`
  description from `"reference + execute inline"` (with inner quotes) to
  `reference-and-execute-inline` to avoid YAML parser error in the generator
  output. Two other files still used the original `"reference + execute inline"`

    * commands/release.md line 10 (dispatch skill mention)

  Both updated to `reference-and-execute-inline` for terminological consistency.
  Neither file goes through the generator wrap, so the YAML defect did not

docs(v2.16.0): patch Codex harness for benign shell artifacts + README exclusion

Two fixes prompted by a real Codex run that hit a false-positive HALT:

(1) HALT condition refinement

Original rule was over-broad: "Any shell command returns a
permission-denied error or asks for credentials." Codex correctly
followed the rule but tripped on a benign WSL/podman artifact:
`mkdir /run/user/1000: permission denied` from bash login-shell
session-init.

The command Codex needed to run (`ls _workflows/*.md | wc -l`)
actually succeeded and returned 13; only the tangential shell-init
message mentioned permission. The HALT was a false positive.

Patch:
- Rewrite HALT rule to require the failure to BLOCK the test:
  "A required command returns a permission-denied error preventing
  the test from completing OR asks for credentials"
- Add explicit "Benign shell artifacts" section listing the common
  patterns (mkdir /run/user/{uid} from bash -lc; podman RunRoot
  warnings; container-runtime advisory) Codex should ignore
- Document the workaround: use plain `bash -c` (no -l) to skip
  systemd session-init entirely

(2) Counter audit commands README exclusion

Original counter audit used `ls _workflows/*.md | wc -l` which
includes README.md and produces 13 instead of the expected 12 (12
workflow definitions + 1 README). Same potential issue in
commands/*.md.

Patch:
- Add `grep -vi readme` filter to commands + workflows counter
  commands (matches the existing subagents/ counter pattern which
  already had grep -vE '_|README')
- Add explicit note explaining the README exclusion rule and how
  to recover if Codex ran the un-filtered version (re-run with the
  filter)

Both fixes are forward-looking: future Codex runs of this harness
on different (or same) environments will not retrip these specific
false positives.

Triggering observation: Codex run paused on Test 2 with HALT after
`bash -lc "ls _workflows/*.md | wc -l"` returned both 13 (the count)
AND the benign shell-init permission warning. Both fixes target the
exact phrase Codex would now interpret correctly.

fix(v2.16.0): wrap {role} placeholder in backticks to escape MDX JSX parsing

CI failure on PR #147 at commit bfd0c41:

  validate (ubuntu-latest) + validate (windows-latest) BOTH FAIL
  Astro build step: ReferenceError: role is not defined
  Error rendering / (docs/index.mdx)

Root cause: docs/index.mdx is .mdx (not .md). MDX parses {role} as a
JSX expression and tries to evaluate 'role' as a JavaScript variable.
Since 'role' is not defined, the build crashes at the homepage render.

The string 'skills/utility-pm-{role}/' was introduced in commit
65a4f2e (Codex P1 fix for dispatch-client-gap-framing) inside the
v2.16.0 row of the Recent Releases table at docs/index.mdx line 267.
The same string appears in 4 .md files (active-orchestration.md,
sub-agents.md, authoring-sub-agents.md, platforms.md) but .md files
do NOT have JSX semantics so they render the literal text correctly.

Fix: wrap the path in backticks to make it a code span. MDX treats
content inside backticks literally (no JSX expression parsing). The
path is semantically a placeholder/example anyway, so a code span is
the appropriate markdown semantics.

Before:
  4 dispatch skills at skills/utility-pm-{role}/ deliver cross-...

After:
  4 dispatch skills at `skills/utility-pm-{role}/` deliver cross-...

Verified .mdx scope:
- docs/index.mdx (this fix)
- docs/showcase/index.mdx (no {placeholder} patterns; clean)

The 5 cascade failures (Astro build crashes -> homepage render
fails -> editLink count drops below threshold of 100 to 46 -> 'Verify
edit-link resolution' check fails) should all clear once the build
succeeds.

Lesson for future: any path placeholder in .mdx files MUST be in
backticks or backslash-escaped. The .md vs .mdx distinction matters
for JSX-style expression parsing.

fix(M-31): robust h2 section parsing in the reciprocity validator (codex C-5)

fix(M-32): make the AGENTS.md --check line-ending agnostic (Windows CI)

The first push surfaced a Windows-only CI failure: "Check AGENTS.md skills catalog
is current" failed on windows-latest while passing on ubuntu. Root cause: the
committed AGENTS.md blob is LF, but .gitattributes marks *.md `text` (no eol=lf), so
the windows runner checks it out as CRLF; gen-skill-manifest.mjs --agents --check
then compared the CRLF file byte-for-byte against the freshly spliced LF block and
read STALE. The content was current (the difference was EOL-only).

Fix: normalize CRLF to LF on both sides of the --check comparison (the AGENTS block
and, defensively, the JSON manifest), mirroring gen-resource-index.mjs which already
normalizes and passed on windows. Added a normalizeEol export plus 2 regression
tests, one reproducing the bug (raw CRLF-vs-LF compare differs; normalized matches).
Verified by forcing AGENTS.md to CRLF locally: --check now reports current.

pm-skill beats freehand (gaps +1.2 to +2.2 where the scenario discriminates), and

fix(v2.27.0): close the 2 G1 adversarial-review findings (fail-closed eval gates)

The codex adversarial review of v2.26.0..HEAD returned needs-attention with two
high findings - both ways the new eval gates could give false confidence. Fixed:

   rows as a gate failure (respecting a deliberate --skills filter), and (b) the
   run fails closed (exit 2) whenever `stopped` is true, after writing the report +
   json for diagnosis. `stopped` is also recorded in the result json.

2. Single-skill output eval omitted the absolute quality gate
   (output-eval.workflow.mjs). It returned only the discrimination + agreement
   gates with no verdict, so a sub-bar or floored skill could read as a pass when
   the control is worse and agreement is low - conflicting with the
   absolute-failure-first contract the batch + informed runners enforce. Now it
   mirrors gateVerdict (floored criteria, absolute_pass, fail/void/pass verdict)
   and returns + logs it.

docs(audit): record the ADR format divergence (external finding EC-1) (#238)

develop-adr emits Nygard-format ADRs while jp-init-project mandates MADR v4
decision records at docs/internal/decisions/. An agent invoking the skill
inside an org repo writes a record that does not match the repo it lands in.
Reported by the maintainer of product-lifecycle-templates, where this is
finding EC-1 (ADR format divergence).

Reported, not patched. The skill's output format is a genuine decision, not
an oversight: develop-adr is a public product and Nygard is the most widely
recognized ADR format, while the MADR mandate governs the org's own internal
records. The audit lays out four options and recommends adding a MADR mode
rather than converting the skill, but leaves the call to the maintainer.

Re-checking each claim against the source (rather than trusting the
originating repo's summary) surfaced two things that finding did not have:

- This repo's own audit README plans "e.g., Nygard format ADRs" for a future
  docs/internal/decisions/ folder. That folder does not exist yet, so
  correcting it costs one line now and a migration later. Left as-is here
  because it is the maintainer's convention call, not a factual error.
- Org-wide MADR adoption is partial, not complete: thinking-framework-skills
  has no tracked decisions folder and no MADR reference at all.

Also fixes verifiable defects in the audit README while indexing the new file:
all three Active-audits links were dead, and the File-naming section claimed a
topic-first de facto pattern that none of the sixteen files in this folder use
(all are date-first). That false claim is what made the links dead.

ci: run validate-plugin on every PR so the required check can report (#244)

`validate-plugin` is a required status check in the `main Protection`
ruleset, but its pull_request trigger carried a paths filter. A PR touching
only site/** or a root package.json never triggered the workflow, so the
required check never reported a conclusion and GitHub returned BLOCKED
permanently, with every visible check green and no failure to point at.

Nine open PRs are stuck this way, eight of them Dependabot updates carrying
open security alerts (four high severity). The last site-only merges landed
2026-07-05, seconds after the ruleset was last edited; nothing site-only has
merged since.

Dropping the filter makes the required check report on every PR. The job runs
in about 20 seconds, so this costs far less than the deadlock. The push
trigger keeps its paths filter, since required-check evaluation applies only
to pull requests.

* fix(site): declare @astrojs/markdown-remark so the astro 7.1 build resolves

Astro 7 replaced the remark/rehype pipeline with its native Markdown
processor and stopped installing @astrojs/markdown-remark by default. The
deprecated `markdown.remarkPlugins` keys in site/astro.config.mjs hard-fail
config validation without that package present.

The site got away with it because @astrojs/markdown-remark arrived
transitively on astro 7.0.2. The 7.1.x tree drops it (594 packages to 567),
so config validation threw before rendering a single page, taking the
enforcing edit-link, rendered-link and route-parity gates down with it as
collateral once site/dist was never created.

Declaring it as a direct dependency fixes the bump and removes the latent
fragility: the site uses remark plugins directly, so it should always have
depended on the package directly.

Verified locally on astro 7.1.6: build completes (415 pages), edit-link
resolution passes (400 targets), rendered-link check passes (428 pages, 0
broken), route parity holds at 428/428, and mermaid markup still renders.

Keeps the deprecated `remarkPlugins` form on purpose. astro-mermaid injects
its own remark/rehype plugins through those same keys, so moving to
`processor: unified({...})` risks silently orphaning them. Documented at the
call site along with why the dependency must not be pruned as unused.

ci: fix nondeterministic false failure in the bash AGENTS.md sync validator (#246)

scripts/validate-agents-md.sh sets `set -euo pipefail` and tested membership
with `printf '%s\n' "${agents_paths[@]}" | grep -Fxq "$path"`. `grep -q` exits
the instant it matches, closing the read end of the pipe, so `printf` can die
with EPIPE. pipefail then promotes that dead printf to a pipeline failure even
though grep matched, and the loop reports a present entry as missing.

It is a race, so it stayed hidden: 14 consecutive main runs passed, and the
same commit passed on its own PR minutes earlier. It fired on main at c33e5f2d
with "printf: write error: Broken pipe" followed by false FAILs for
define-jtbd-canvas and define-problem-statement, both of which are present in
AGENTS.md. The PowerShell leg passed on identical content, so the two shells
disagreed on a repo that was actually correct.

0.41.0's extend merging the built-in default still applied, so the shadow was

regressions), and the user declaration now genuinely wins: every page without
explicit `draft:` frontmatter gets `undefined` instead of `false`.

false` (strict equality), so all 428 collection entries were dropped,
`routes` was empty, and the build died on the first sidebar slug lookup:

changelog item only moved the same error to `skills`.

the default and validates tags.md's `draft: true`. A comment now marks the

fix(memory): the documented config now parses, and the coverage claim is now asserted

Three findings from the G1 adversarial review of the v2.32.0 release content, all
verified against the files before acting. Two were defects in this release; one
was an undocumented format.

1. The published config example did not work (ship-blocking). The frontmatter
   reader did not strip trailing YAML comments, and the example shipped in
   concepts/hooks.md carries them, so a user copying it verbatim got
   `memoryPhase = null`: the router silently fell back to heuristics and the
   active initiative was suppressed with it. Reproduced, then fixed in the
   reader rather than the doc, because a comment is valid YAML and users write
   them. Comment stripping is quote- and list-aware, so `issue#42`,
   `"Sprint #14 cleanup"` and `[a, b] # note` all survive. Blast radius checked
   first: frontmatter.mjs has two callers, phase-map reads only `phase` and
   `name`, and no skill frontmatter value contains a space-hash.

   The regression test reads the REAL doc file and parses the example out of it,
   rather than a hand-copied fixture. Every prior test wrote its own input, which
   is exactly why nothing caught this: the parser was only ever tested against
   what its author wrote, never against what users copy.

2. "53 + 15 = 68, asserted in test so it cannot drift" was not true. The test
   asserted `ROSTER.length === 53` and no duplicates; the accounting lived in a
   comment. EXCLUDED was exported but imported nowhere and skill-manifest.json
   was never consulted, so a 69th skill added to neither list left the suite
   green while the published claim silently became false. Now asserted for real:
   exact set equality between the catalog and the disjoint union of roster and
   exclusions, in both directions, plus no duplicates, plus every excluded name
   must be tool-classified so the exclusion cannot become a dumping ground.
   Falsified before trusting it: injecting a phantom 69th skill fails the suite
   with the intended message, and the manifest was restored byte-identical.

   This claim had been published in CONTRIBUTING, the evals page, the release
   plan, and two issue comments. The fix makes the claim true rather than
   weakening the prose, so those surfaces are now accurate as written.

3. The `artifacts[]` format was not publicly documented. concepts/hooks.md
   mentioned "artifacts" once, about the router heuristic, while the only real
   definition sat in an unreleased internal spec, even though shipped skill
   contracts write and read tagged artifacts. Since nothing normalizes the file
   at runtime, two skills inventing different shapes cannot hand off, which is
   the whole feature. Now documents the entry shape, required and optional
   fields, the four provenance tags, why `## Decisions` stays prose, and states
   the concurrency limit plainly rather than implying safety.

docs(v2.33.0): pre-register D23, the gate's stopping condition, before round 12

Eleven G1 rounds have run without any committed rule saying when the gate
ends. The round-4 standard at e32a117d governs how findings are
dispositioned; it never says how many rounds are enough. D23 fills that
gap, and it is committed before round 12 launches for the same reason C-2
was ruled VOID against f4d50837 and D17 was ruled before round 4: a
stopping condition chosen after the evidence arrives is a moved goalpost,
and the exposure runs in both directions.

Three measurements were taken before the options were framed, because the
obvious stopping conditions turn on them.

Fix-pass damage is near-universal and is not decaying. Rounds 7 through 11
produced 21 findings and 17 came from the immediately preceding fix pass:
3 of 4, 3 of 4, 4 of 5, 5 of 5, 2 of 3. Every round.

The fix passes are not shrinking. Diff sizes for the round-6 through
round-11 fixes run 91, 128, 51, 141, 95, 86 lines changed. Flat, not
tapering.

Together these falsify any rule of the form "recheck until a recheck comes
back clean". Each fix pass is the same size as the last and carries the
same damage rate, so the expected number of further rounds under an
open-ended rule is unbounded. A gate needs a terminator that does not
depend on a clean round arriving. This is the round-9 lesson reached from
the other side: fixes that delete a claim converged, fixes that author
methodology churned, and D22's authored replacement then churned twice
more at R10-F1 and R11-F1.

The third measurement corrects an earlier draft of this brief. Untouched
territory produced findings in rounds 6 through 11 at 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1:
three of six rounds and declining, not the four of six the draft claimed
and used as its case against option B. The correction is recorded in the
brief rather than quietly removed, because it weakens an argument the
brief was making for its own recommendation.

D23 = A. One scoped recheck of 51d5bec6, pre-registered as the last
adversarial round of this gate. Whatever it returns: changed-surface
findings are closed, untouched-territory findings are deferred to v2.34.0
under clause 2, the resulting fix pass is verified by a recorded
finding-versus-result table rather than by another round, and the gate is
attested. Termination is by construction.

The option set had to cover two damage classes the records already
separate. Execution fidelity, where the fix did not do everything the
finding named, is R11-F2's class at its third recurrence and is catchable
by a mechanical re-read. Fresh design damage, where the replacement itself
has a new hole, is R9-F1/F2, R10-F1 and R11-F1, and only adversarial
review sees it. 51d5bec6 contains one change of each: the trace row split
is design, the quote-editing marker is fidelity.

Option D, direct verification of the three round-11 fixes with no
adversarial round, is recorded and rejected on that split. It covers
fidelity only, and the row split is exactly the class it cannot see,
because a replacement can be a faithful implementation of the finding and
still carry a new hole. D is absorbed into A as the verification
instrument for A's own fix pass, where the residual risk really is

Instruments are named in the brief so the round cannot be re-litigated on
method. Codex companion adversarial-review is the instrument of record. A
multi-lens Claude panel runs alongside as a corroborating instrument, its
lenses mapped to the two damage classes plus a governance class-check.
Corroboration adds findings and never subtracts them.

The standing cross-LLM rule, re-run until findings fall below IMPORTANT,
is set aside for this gate's closure on the maintainer's authority as its
owner, mirroring the D17 move. It is an open-ended rule and measurements 1

docs(v2.33.0): G1 CLOSED on maintainer attestation; twelve rounds, one measurement

Attestation GIVEN 2026-08-29, the first and only one sought in this gate.
Rounds 2 through 11 each recorded NOT GIVEN and not sought, because none
was the last round. D23 made round 12 the last, so the attestation is the
act that closes G1.

The record states plainly what is and is not being attested. Not that the
artifact is defect-free: round 12 returned three findings and the
corroborating panel eighteen, five deferred rather than fixed, and the
deferral list names a template row that drops a requirement SKILL.md
makes. What is attested is that findings are dispositioned rather than
unexamined, deferrals are written down with reasons and carried to a named
release, and remaining gaps are recorded as gaps instead of hidden behind
a checked box.

Final trend 5, 6, 8, 6, 6, 6, 4, 4, 5, 5, 3, 3. Fifty-six findings across
twelve rounds.

The measurement worth outliving this release: splitting all fifty-six by
what the fix that produced the surface did separates them completely.
Fixes that deleted a claim converged every time; the evaluation-sizing
block produced zero findings across the nine rounds after D15 deleted its
derivation. Fixes that authored methodology or structure churned every
time; the trace block survived a symmetric rewrite, a choreography
deletion with an authored replacement, and a row split, and produced a
fresh high after each.

R12-F1 is the cleanest instance in the gate: the fix that split a row to
assert one-claim-per-row authored a row carrying two. The principle was
right and embodying it in authored structure reintroduced the defect one
level down.

Plan status moves to READY TO TAG, not SHIPPED. SHIPPED belongs at G3 when
a tag exists; stamping it earlier is the same pre-satisfied-control defect
that R11-F3 and R12-F3 both caught in this cycle's own checklist.
